subject: Order form commercial alignment — entity carveout, net terms, VAT treatment
messages:
From: Marco Rossi <mrossi@intellisys.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Accounting <ap@intellisys.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: IntelliSys draft order form (redline attached)

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. I've attached our redline of the proposed order form (IntelliSys_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf) — the commercial team flagged a few items we need clarified before procurement will accept:

- Pricing schedule: we need a clearer breakdown by environment (prod vs staging) and a quarterly reconciliation for overage charges.
- Minimum commit: our legal team prefers the commit split across two entities (IntelliSys S.p.A and IntelliSys UK Ltd). Can Redwood invoice and allocate commits to two legal entities?
- Net terms: procurement is pushing Net 60 on the full value; finance asks for Net 30.
- VAT/responsibility: EU VAT handling needs to be explicit; who is responsible for VAT when the billing entity is non-EU?

Can you confirm which of the above are acceptable as-is and which need a contract amendment? I've copied Accounting for the invoice path discussion.

Attached: IntelliSys_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf

Best,
Marco Rossi
Head of Cloud Engineering
IntelliSys

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marco Rossi <mrossi@intellisys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: IntelliSys draft order form (redline attached)

Marco — thanks for the clear callouts and for sharing the redline. Quick summary from our side and proposed next steps so procurement has something concrete: 

1) Pricing schedule and env breakdown
- We can include a line-item split for Production vs Staging in the order form pricing schedule. That will be reflected as separate invoice lines and will appear in the monthly usage report for reconciliation.

2) Minimum commit split across entities
- Redwood can accept a split of commits across multiple invoicing entities, but we need: (a) entity-specific order forms (or an appendix that maps commit % to entity legal names and tax IDs), and (b) a primary billing entity specified for account-level obligations.
- Operationally this means we will generate separate invoices to each entity based on the agreed percent allocation and apply commits against those entity-specific invoices.

3) Net terms
- Our standard is Net 30. For Net 60 we need an approval from Finance and a credit review. Ben, can you advise on any precedent for Net 45/60 on enterprise deals of this size?

4) VAT treatment
- For EU customers: if invoiced from our non-EU entity, VAT responsibility typically falls to the buyer under reverse-charge rules — we can put explicit language in the order form. If IntelliSys prefers Redwood to handle VAT and remit, we need to route invoices from Redwood EU entity and may need an entity-level VAT registration. Laura, can you confirm EU entity readiness?

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood will produce an "Entity Allocation Appendix" draft and an updated pricing schedule (separate line items for prod/staging).
- Ben/Legal will weigh in on Net terms approval path and any changes needed to payment SLA.
- Laura will confirm if Redwood EU invoicing is available (so we can pick VAT-remit option).

I'll attach a one-page appendix template to the redline and send an updated order form for IntelliSys review by EOD tomorrow. Does that timeline work?

Thanks — Kimberly
Director, GTM Finance Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marco Rossi <mrossi@intellisys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: IntelliSys draft order form (redline attached)

Looping in some legal/finance specifics.

Marco / Kimberly — quick points from my side (Legal + Sales ops):

- Entity split: we can do the allocation appendix but two notes: (1) we need signatures from both IntelliSys entities on the appendix, and (2) the MSA must reference the appendix by version to avoid mismatch on commits vs billing.

- Overage reconciliation: we'll add a quarterly reconciliation clause that allows IntelliSys to true-up overages against the commit at quarter end; overage rates will match the line-item pricing unless a separate agreement is noted.

- Net terms: Net 30 is default. For Net 60, Finance will require either (a) a prepayment of first quarter, or (b) an approved credit holdback mechanism. We will put both options in the appendix so procurement can choose.

- VAT: we recommend issuing EU invoices from Redwood's EU entity when possible to simplify VAT. If IntelliSys insists on UK or Italian invoicing split, we need local tax IDs from you and will pass to Accounting to configure.

I'll flag to Legal to accept the redline with the above amendments. Kimberly — please attach the draft appendix and the updated pricing schedule when you send the next version.

Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Marco Rossi <mrossi@intellisys.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Accounting <ap@intellisys.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: IntelliSys draft order form (redline attached)

Thanks, Ben/Kimberly — that all sounds reasonable. A couple of clarifications from our procurement/tax lead: 

- We will provide local tax IDs for both entities by Monday.
- Procurement prefers Net 45 if possible; they'll accept Net 60 only with prepayment of Q1 as you mentioned. Net 45 would be our default ask.
- On VAT: IntelliSys would prefer Redwood to invoice from EU entity to avoid reverse-charge complexity. If that's not possible right away, we can accept split invoicing with clear VAT line items, but it's a higher operational lift for our AP team.

Can you include Net 45 as an option in the appendix so procurement can sign off faster?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Marco

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marco Rossi <mrossi@intellisys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Accounting <ap@intellisys.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: IntelliSys draft order form (redline attached)

Marco — great, thanks for the confirmation. Finalizing action items and timeline below: 

Action items:
- Redwood: send updated order form + Entity Allocation Appendix + pricing schedule with Prod/Staging line items (attached). Will include Net 30 / Net 45 / Net 60 (with prepay option) as selectable payment terms in the appendix. (Deliverable: Updated_OrderForm_IntelliSys_v4.pdf; ETA: EOD 14 Jul)
- IntelliSys: provide legal names and tax IDs for both entities and indicate preferred net term (Net 30/45/60) by Monday 17 Jul. (Marco / AP)
- Accounting (Redwood): Laura will confirm EU invoicing availability. If EU invoicing is immediately available, Redwood will route EU invoices to IntelliSys and assume VAT remit per normal EU invoicing rules; otherwise we'll default to split invoicing with VAT lines.
- Legal (Ben): will prepare the finalized MSA reference to the appendix and confirm signature flow (both entities may need to sign appendix).

Attachments: Updated_OrderForm_IntelliSys_v4.pdf; Entity_Allocation_Appendix_template.docx; pricing-breakdown-intellisys.xlsx

Marco — please confirm timeline works and whether procurement needs a short companion note explaining the VAT options (we can draft for you).

Thanks — Kimberly
Director, GTM Finance Ops
Redwood Inference
